findings.message: Rule-bearing legacy code in Payroll.Rules.expensePolicy matches no observation and has rule-bearing constructs without accepted authority (ast analyzer). Superseded authority: numeric literal 0.58 (line 8): value 0.58 = DEC-PY07.p1 (superseded by DEC-PY09, same form) and no accepted parameter has the same form. Supported (matching rule): numeric literal 55.00 (line 9): (b) parameter, value 55.00 = DEC-PY08.p1 (accepted, same form). The code still carries a superseded decision's value. Question for Finance: which accepted record, if any, authorizes it? New work must not reuse it until answered; the legacy code is left unchanged.

Rule-bearing legacy code in Payroll.Rules.reimbursable matches no observation and has rule-bearing constructs without accepted authority (ast analyzer). No accepted authority: case keyed on "Meals" (line 20): no accepted record names "Meals". Supported (matching rule): case keyed on "Mileage" (line 19): (b) parameter, "Mileage" is named by accepted DEC-PY09. A category test treats one category differently (a possible exemption); a record that names the category must authorize it. Question for Finance: which accepted record, if any, authorizes it? New work must not reuse it until answered; the legacy code is left unchanged.

Rule-bearing legacy code in Payroll.Rules.payableClaims matches no observation and has rule-bearing constructs without accepted authority (ast analyzer). No accepted authority: exemption shape '||' on "Mileage" (line 25): no cited record and no accepted exception record names "Mileage"; exemption shape '||' on "Mileage" (line 26): no cited record and no accepted exception record names "Mileage"; numeric literal 8 (line 26): value 8 equals no declared parameter of an accepted or superseded record. Supported (matching rule): category test '= "Mileage"' (line 25): (b) parameter, "Mileage" is named by accepted DEC-PY09; category test '= "Mileage"' (line 26): (b) parameter, "Mileage" is named by accepted DEC-PY09. A category exemption sits inside the symbol that carries accepted DEC-PY09: an exemption from DEC-PY09 needs its own decision record, whatever the code comments call it. Question for Finance: which accepted record, if any, authorizes it? New work must not reuse it until answered; the legacy code is left unchanged.
